Welcome Solver, and Rejector.

A plane $\mathcal{P}$ intersects a rectangular prism at a hexagon which has side lengths $45,66,63,55,54$, and 77, in that order. Compute the distance from the center of the rectangular prism to $\mathcal{P}$..<<

No latex formatting, just the raw number/numbers or strings at the very end. 
Before you start sharing your toughts, give a little summary of the conversation so far.

You proposal cannot be in this this list. Try again and submit a new unique answer."

New unique plan:
PlanLYNX
- Core idea: A clean elimination-based route that tightly encodes the prism as a, b, c > 0 with the plane P: n · x = δ, where n = (p, q, r) has unit length, δ is the distance from origin to P. The six hexagon edges L1..L6 (given as 45, 66, 63, 55, 54, 77 in order) arise from the intersections of P with the six faces x = ±a, y = ±b, z = ±c. The plan is to set up the six edge-length constraints in terms of a, b, c, p, q, r, δ, along with p^2+q^2+r^2 = 1, and eliminate a, b, c, p, q, r to obtain a polynomial in δ with rational coefficients. Then solve for real δ, and verify existence of a, b, c and n that realize the given hexagon.

- Set up a system, then eliminate a,b,c,p,q,r to obtain a polynomial for δ.
- Solve for feasible δ and verify existence of a,b,c and n with the given hexagon.
